name: Machine Learning & Its Math — The Faculties of Mind, Made Buildable
thesis: Understand and build the core of modern ML — the math you actually need, then neural nets, embeddings, diffusion, attention, and training. Intuition first, code second, math demystified.

what_is_ml.hook: A normal program: you write the rules. ML flips it. What does the machine produce that you DIDN'T write?
what_is_ml.recall: What does an ML model learn, vs a normal program?
what_is_ml.answer: it learns the rules/patterns FROM data, instead of you coding them

ml_types.hook: Three ways a machine learns: one has answers, one finds hidden structure, one learns by reward. Name them.
ml_types.recall: Supervised vs unsupervised vs RL — one line each?
ml_types.answer: supervised = learn from labeled examples; unsupervised = find structure in unlabeled data; RL = learn by reward

vectors.hook: A word, an image, a user — ML turns each into the same thing: a list of numbers. What's that list called?
vectors.recall: What is a vector, and why is everything in ML one?
vectors.answer: an ordered list of numbers; it places any 'thing' as a point in space so math can work on it

dot_product.hook: How does a machine decide two things are 'similar'? One tiny operation does it.
dot_product.recall: What does the dot product tell you about two vectors?
dot_product.answer: how aligned/similar they are — the basis of similarity

gradient.hook: The model is wrong. Which way should it nudge its numbers to be LESS wrong? What points the way?
gradient.recall: What does a gradient tell a model?
gradient.answer: the direction (and steepness) to change the weights to reduce the error

neuron.hook: All of deep learning is one tiny unit, repeated. What does a single neuron actually do?
neuron.answer: a weighted sum of its inputs, then a nonlinearity (activation)

network_layers.hook: Stack neurons into layers and something powerful appears. What can a deep network represent?
network_layers.recall: What is a neural network, in essence?
network_layers.answer: a function approximator — it learns to map inputs to outputs

forward_pass.hook: Data goes in, a prediction comes out. What's that left-to-right computation called?
forward_pass.recall: What happens in the forward pass?
forward_pass.answer: inputs flow through the layers to produce a prediction

loss.hook: Before a model can improve, it must know HOW wrong it is. What turns 'wrong' into a number?
loss.answer: a number measuring how far the prediction is from the target

backprop.hook: The error shows up at the output — but the blame lives in weights deep inside. How does it travel back?
backprop.answer: sends the error backward through the network to compute each weight's gradient

training_loop.hook: Learning is one loop run thousands of times. Name its steps.
training_loop.recall: The steps of the training loop?
training_loop.answer: forward -> compute loss -> backprop -> update weights, repeat

tensors.hook: PyTorch's basic object holds your data AND runs on a GPU. What is it?
tensors.answer: a multi-dimensional array (like a vector/matrix) that can run on CPU or GPU

autograd.hook: You coded backprop by hand once. PyTorch hands it to you free. What feature?
autograd.answer: automatic differentiation — it computes the gradients for you

embeddings.hook: How can a machine 'know' king - man + woman ≈ queen? Meaning becomes what?
embeddings.answer: a vector that holds meaning as geometry — similar things sit close together

vector_search.hook: Millions of embeddings, one query. How do you find the closest meaning, fast?
vector_search.answer: find the nearest vectors (cosine/distance) to a query — semantic retrieval

autoencoder.hook: Squeeze an image down to a few numbers, then rebuild it. What learns that compressed essence?
autoencoder.answer: to encode data into a small latent code and decode it back — the essence of the data

diffusion.hook: Start from pure noise and denoise step by step into a picture. What family of model is that?
diffusion.recall: How does a diffusion model generate an image?
diffusion.answer: it learns to reverse noise — denoising step by step from random noise into data

attention.hook: To understand a word, a model must look at the RIGHT other words. What mechanism lets it?
attention.answer: lets the model weigh which other tokens matter for each token

transformer.hook: The architecture behind every LLM. What's it built from?
transformer.recall: What is a transformer built from?
transformer.answer: stacked attention + feed-forward blocks, processing all tokens in parallel (no recurrence)

overfitting.hook: Your model aces the training data but flops on new data. What's that — and one fix?
overfitting.recall: What is overfitting, and one way to fight it?
overfitting.answer: memorizing training data instead of generalizing; fix with more data / regularization / dropout

evaluation.hook: How do you KNOW the model is good, not just lucky?
evaluation.recall: How do you properly evaluate a model?
evaluation.answer: test on held-out data it never trained on, with the right metric
